facts.fact: Hakam is the three-fingered old man of Kothi Shilak whom Meera points out in the yard.
facts.why: needed because Meera's reply to Rohan's ear question uses a concrete villager as evidence that the whole village has lost something to the pass.

facts.fact: Rohan's party for the crossing is two wardens (Rohan and Varun) and two guides (Jassi and Meera); the other wardens return to the post.
facts.why: needed because the beat pairs Rohan with Jassi and Meera with Varun, and ch 3 shows only those four plus goats.

facts.fact: Rohan has told Varun, and no one else beyond the queen, that he carries the queen's seal.
facts.why: needed because Asha knows the seal exists through Varun (bible); implied by Rohan's interiority that Varun is a trusted second. Not stated explicitly on the page, only implied by his trust.

facts.fact: Wardens carry an iron probe spike used to find salt in grain; the salt house wool bales were probed to arm's depth with it but not cut open.
facts.why: needed because the beat has Rohan search thoroughly yet not find the redbark hidden in the heart of a bale.

facts.fact: Varun's coat has one new brass button among pewter ones; he claims a pedlar sold it to him after he lost a button on the stair.
facts.why: needed to plant C22 (the twin of Meera's button) as a Rohan-visible detail without Meera seeing it.

facts.fact: Widow Puja's seizure fine is eighteen silver, for salt found in her late husband's lean-to; Rohan pays it secretly.
facts.why: needed to make the kindness (C23) concrete; amount and cause invented.

facts.fact: Meera tells the yard her mother died of the grey cough ten winters ago because medicine was on the wrong side of the law.
facts.why: needed to ground her answer in the bible's timeline (mother dies of fever in a closed winter ten winters before Book 1); it is public knowledge to Rohan from this chapter.
